concerns.text: T006 requires "4 transform incl. baseline" JSON files and T008 requires aggregated CSV rows "including the untransformed baseline", but the aggregated_result schema's `transformation` enum allows only box_cox/yeo_johnson/rank_based with additionalProperties:false. The baseline rows T008 must emit cannot conform to the contract the task cites — the task is not executable as specified. Add a `baseline`/`none` enum value (or specify the baseline's representation) before T006/T008 can run.

T002 writes one datasets.csv row per downloaded dataset (≥50, pre-filter), but the schema requires sample_size minimum 30 and missing_pct maximum 10 on every row. Datasets that will later be excluded for N<30 or >10% missing cannot be recorded, so the download task's own verification (`len(df)>=50`) conflicts with the contract it must conform to. Specify a raw-metadata schema or relax the constraints for pre-filter rows.

T003 excludes datasets with "no continuous variable" and updates datasets.csv with `filter_reason`, but the enum only permits normal/small_n/missing_too_high/no_group. The no-continuous-variable exclusion required by the spec's Dataset-variable fit assumption cannot be written per contract; T003's update step is unexecutable for that case.

The OpenML API query is given as `https://www.openml.org/api/v1/json/data/list/limit/200/...` — literally truncated with "...". An implementer cannot deterministically reconstruct the filter parameters (status/quality/feature-type filters) from this. Either give the full query string or mandate the "fixed list of verified OpenML dataset IDs ≥50 in length" as the sole mechanism (and state where that list lives).

T005 writes the pilot summary to `data/results/type1_error_pilot.json`, placing results under `data/` while every other task and the plan's structure use `results/` as the results root. Pick one location so the T012 results.md linkage and verification paths are unambiguous.

Verification demands "re-running the plotting step reproduces byte-identical figures". matplotlib PNG output embeds creation metadata by default; byte-identity requires explicitly setting metadata/timestamps off (e.g. `metadata={"Software": None}` and fixed SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH). The task should name this requirement or soften to content-identity (e.g. identical array hash), otherwise the check may spuriously fail.
